================================================================================
PART 1: README
================================================================================

# PROTEUS

The terminal is where every command passes. So make it the system of record.

A GPU terminal for Windows that remembers every session, sees every process, undoes shell commands, and gives AI agents a real terminal to drive over MCP. One 22 MB exe (16.9 MB in the measured ledger entry forge/ledger.json#L52). No install.

Links:
- Download PROTEUS.exe: https://github.com/karimalsalah/proteus/releases/latest/download/PROTEUS.exe
- Repository: https://github.com/karimalsalah/proteus
- Releases: https://github.com/karimalsalah/proteus/releases
- Roadmap: https://github.com/karimalsalah/proteus/blob/main/forge/roadmap.md
- Ledger: https://github.com/karimalsalah/proteus/blob/main/forge/ledger.json
- Media: docs/media/world.gif — A real `cargo build` (and one that fails), replayed from its journal in the world view. Every node is a process the session started, with its command line and exit code, reported by Windows itself. Nothing in this picture is drawn for decoration.

## Why

Every command you run, and every command your AI agents run, goes through a terminal. Today the terminal forgets all of it the moment it scrolls away. It cannot tell you what a build spawned, which process failed, what the screen said ten minutes ago, or how to put the files back.

PROTEUS keeps all of that:

- It remembers. Every session is journaled with timestamps. Any past instant renders exactly, in milliseconds.
- It senses. Windows reports every process a session starts (command line, parent, exit code, CPU time) through a job object. No shell hooks.
- It undoes. `proteus run -- <cmd>` snapshots the working tree before and after. `proteus chronicle undo` puts it back.
- It serves agents. `proteus mcp` gives any MCP client sessions it can spawn, type into, wait on without polling, read without noise, and see as images.
- It costs nothing when idle. 0.00% CPU and zero frames drawn while nothing changes, measured on every build.

## What it does

- Time travel (docs/media/scrub.png): Ctrl+Shift+Left steps back through a session, output event by output event. The bar is the session's real output rate over its whole life. Keyframes make any instant reachable in milliseconds; `proteus recall find TEXT` says when text was on screen.
- Light from real events (docs/media/reveal.gif): Text that lands in an empty cell unfolds and casts light in its own colour. Spinners and in-place edits swap instantly, so an agent's busy indicator costs 9 frames a second, not 100. Nothing animates when nothing happens.
- Drawn by the engine (docs/media/draw.png): Box drawing (light, heavy, rounded, double, mixed junctions), blocks, braille and powerline are drawn by the GPU, not the font, so they join perfectly at any size. Undercurl is a real wave; dotted and dashed underlines take their own colour.
- Sessions outlive windows: A daemon inside the same exe holds sessions. Close the window, open another, and it picks up exactly where you were.
- Undo for the shell: Content-addressed history of the working tree. Restore is a dry run until you pass `--apply`, never follows links out of the tree, and snapshots first.
- Sound from events: A tick per key, a grain for arriving text, a chime for the bell, rising for success and falling for failure. Computed, not sampled. The audio device sleeps between sounds.
- Protocols: Kitty keyboard protocol (real Shift+Enter for agent UIs), synchronized output, colour queries, OSC 7501 program status (agents that report their state start doing so).
- Self-updating: Checks once a day for a newer release, verifies its Ed25519 signature, size and hash, and applies it at next launch. No downgrades. `"update": "off"` turns it off.
- Eyes and ears: `proteus shot` renders any session, journal or moment to PNG with no window. `proteus ears` renders every sound to WAV. Agents can look at what they did.

Every number on this page has a command that produced it in `forge/ledger.json`. The rule in this repository: a claim without a measurement does not get written down.

## Install

Direct: download `PROTEUS.exe` (https://github.com/karimalsalah/proteus/releases/latest/download/PROTEUS.exe) and run it. That is the whole install. It unpacks what it needs (console host, fonts) into `%LOCALAPPDATA%\proteus` on first run and updates itself after that.

Scoop:
```powershell
scoop install https://raw.githubusercontent.com/karimalsalah/proteus/main/packaging/scoop/proteus.json
```

Windows SmartScreen will say "unknown publisher" on first run: the exe is not yet signed with a Windows code-signing certificate. Choose More info -> Run anyway, or check the download against the signed `PROTEUS.manifest` in the release.

## For AI agents

PROTEUS is an MCP server. It gives an agent what a person has at a terminal: a real pseudo-console, a screen to look at, and patience.

| Tool | What it does |
|---|---|
| `spawn` | Start a program on a real terminal; a person can watch it live with `proteus --attach N` |
| `send` | Type text and named keys; returns a cursor into the output |
| `wait` | Block until a regex matches, output goes quiet, or the program exits. Event-driven, not polling |
| `read` | Output since a cursor, lean: escape codes stripped, progress bars collapsed to their final state, repeats folded, errors never dropped, with raw and lean byte counts |
| `screen` / `shot` | The screen as text or as a PNG, now or as it stood at any earlier moment |
| `sessions` / `kill` | List and end sessions. By default an agent drives only sessions it started |

Claude Desktop: download `proteus-mcp.mcpb` from the latest release (https://github.com/karimalsalah/proteus/releases/latest) and open it.

Claude Code (or any MCP client):
```powershell
claude mcp add --scope user --transport stdio proteus -- "C:\path\to\PROTEUS.exe" mcp
```

It is listed in the MCP Registry (https://registry.modelcontextprotocol.io/) as `io.github.karimalsalah/proteus`.

## Use

```powershell
proteus                          # a window on a new session, or the one you left
proteus sessions                 # what the daemon is running
proteus run -- cargo test        # one undoable step
proteus chronicle undo           # dry run; add --apply to perform it
proteus procs --journal F --tree # every process a session started
proteus recall find "error[E"    # when it was on screen
proteus shot --journal F --until 90 --out then.png
proteus update --check           # is there a newer signed release
```

Keys:
- Ctrl+Shift+W: world view
- Ctrl+Shift+Left/Right: step through time (Home/End: start, now)
- Ctrl+Shift+D: detach (session keeps running)
- Ctrl+Shift+Delete: reset the keyboard protocol if a program died with it on

Settings live in `%LOCALAPPDATA%\proteus\config.json`: `font_pt`, `reveal`, `light`, `sound`, `volume`, `update`, `shell`, journal retention.

## What is not done

PROTEUS is early: one person's daily terminal, built in the open. Please read this before trusting it with anything.

- Three views have not been driven by a person yet. The world view, time scrubbing and `--attach` are tested headless through `proteus shot` (that is how the images above were made). Issue #5 (https://github.com/karimalsalah/proteus/issues/5) asks for the first real try.
- Agents' own tool commands are seen as processes, not as output. Harnesses run each command in a separate process. Routing them into PROTEUS sessions is issue #3 (https://github.com/karimalsalah/proteus/issues/3).
- Command boundaries are built but not switched on (issue #1: https://github.com/karimalsalah/proteus/issues/1), and agent status is answered but not shown (issue #2: https://github.com/karimalsalah/proteus/issues/2).
- Undo covers files in the tracked tree only. Not network, registry, databases or anything in `.gitignore`.
- No colour emoji, ligatures or images yet. Journals are plaintext and hold everything printed, including command lines.
- Windows only. No sandbox. PROTEUS observes; it does not contain.
- Nobody has tuned the sound or the light by ear and eye.

The roadmap (https://github.com/karimalsalah/proteus/blob/main/forge/roadmap.md) ranks what comes next, each item with the number that proves it worked and the reading that means drop it.

## Build

Windows 11, Rust (MSVC toolchain).

```powershell
cargo build --release            # target\release\proteus.exe is the whole product
cargo test --release
pwsh forge\gate.ps1 -SkipBench   # the headless gate: tests, runs-alone check, sound, screenshots
pwsh forge\gate.ps1              # full gate: real keys into a test window, bench, idle budget
```

## Contributing

The good first issues (https://github.com/karimalsalah/proteus/issues?q=is%3Aopen+label%3A%22good+first+issue%22) are small and self-contained. Read CONTRIBUTING.md: measured claims only, nothing mock in tests, the gate must pass, and say plainly what you did not test. Questions and ideas go in Discussions (https://github.com/karimalsalah/proteus/discussions).

## Licence

MIT (LICENSE). PROTEUS embeds Microsoft's ConPTY (MIT) and Maple Mono NF (SIL OFL 1.1). `proteus licenses` prints every bundled notice, including all 178 Rust dependencies.

================================================================================
PART 2: AGENTS.md
================================================================================

# AGENTS.md

Instructions for AI coding agents (Codex, Claude Code, Cursor, Copilot, Aider and others) working in this repository. The full working agreement is in CLAUDE.md; this is the short version.

- Build and test: `cargo build --release`, `cargo test --release`, `pwsh forge\gate.ps1 -SkipBench` (headless; opens no window).
- Never open a PROTEUS window from a test or script unless `PROTEUS_NO_FOCUS=1` is set, and always set `PROTEUS_DATA` and `PROTEUS_SOCKET` to a temp folder and `PROTEUS_SOUND=off`, so a person's own sessions are never touched.
- Never kill processes by name. The person may be running PROTEUS itself.
- Measured claims only. Any number you write (in code comments, docs, the ledger, a pull request) comes from a command you ran; put the command beside it.
- Nothing mock. Tests use real processes, real files in temp directories, real journals.
- Look at what you draw: render with `proteus shot ... --out x.png` and read the PNG after any renderer change.
- Update `forge/ledger.json` in the same change: what is done with its evidence, what is known to be wrong.
- Restore and undo delete files. Their tests run only in temp directories.

Using PROTEUS as a tool rather than changing it: `proteus mcp` is an MCP server (sessions, spawn, send, wait, read, screen, shot, kill). See the README section "For AI agents".

================================================================================
PART 3: AGENT TOOLS SECTION (proteus mcp)
================================================================================

Transport: `proteus mcp` over stdio
MCP Registry ID: `io.github.karimalsalah/proteus`
Claude Desktop bundle: `proteus-mcp.mcpb` (in https://github.com/karimalsalah/proteus/releases/latest)
Claude Code registration:
`claude mcp add --scope user --transport stdio proteus -- "C:\path\to\PROTEUS.exe" mcp`

Exposed MCP Tools:
1. `sessions` — List the terminal sessions the daemon is running.
2. `spawn` — Start a program on a real terminal and get its session number; a person can watch it live with `proteus --attach N`.
3. `send` — Type text and named keys into a session; returns a cursor into the output.
4. `wait` — Block until output matches a regex, goes quiet, or the program exits. Event-driven, not polling.
5. `read` — Output since a cursor, lean (escape codes stripped, progress bars collapsed to their final state, repeats folded, errors never dropped, with raw and lean byte counts) or raw.
6. `screen` — The screen as text, now or as it stood at any earlier moment.
7. `shot` — The screen as a PNG image, now or as it stood at any earlier moment.
8. `kill` — End a session. By default an agent drives only sessions it started.

Safety properties:
- By default an agent drives only sessions it started.
- Replayed history cannot answer terminal queries, ring, or write the clipboard (`forge/ledger.json#L49`).
